CLEVELAND--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Cleveland-Cliffs Inc. (NYSE:CLF) today announced that it has reached new four-year labor agreements with the United Steelworkers (USW) across its operating footprint. The agreements cover approximately 12,000 USW-represented employees across the Company’s steel plants and mining operations in Indiana, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Minnesota, and Michigan. The agreements resolve all USW labor contracts currently up for renewal.

Lourenco Goncalves, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Cleveland-Cliffs, said: “Our USW-represented employees do work that is essential to Cleveland-Cliffs and to our country. These agreements recognize their contributions and give us the stability we need to invest, compete and continue strengthening American steelmaking. We greatly value our partnership with the USW and its leadership, whose constructive approach allowed us to reach agreements that benefit our employees and Cliffs.”

The new four-year agreements are subject to ratification by USW local union memberships.

About Cleveland-Cliffs Inc.

Cleveland-Cliffs is a leading North America-based steel producer with focus on value-added sheet products, particularly for the automotive industry. The Company is vertically integrated from the mining of iron ore, production of pellets and direct reduced iron, and processing of ferrous scrap through primary steelmaking and downstream finishing, stamping, tooling, and tubing. Headquartered in Cleveland, Ohio, Cleveland-Cliffs employs approximately 25,000 people across its operations in the United States and Canada.

TEMPE, Ariz. & SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Align Technology, Inc. (“Align”) (Nasdaq: ALGN), a leading global medical device company that designs, manufactures, and sells the Invisalign® System of clear aligners, iTero™ intraoral scanners, and exocad™ CAD/CAM software for digital orthodontics and restorative dentistry, today announced recognition in the 2026 All-America Executive Team rankings published by Extel Insights (formerly Institutional Investor Research), which evaluates the quality of investor relations programs, leadership, and governance as voted on by the buy- and sell-side analyst community. In the Health Care Technology & Distribution sector, Align earned first- and second-place rankings across three Large-Cap award categories – Best CEO, Best IR Program, and Best Investor Day – in both the Combined and Buy-side results. The 2026 awards mark Align’s fourth recognition in five years in the Extel All-America Executive Team rankings, reflecting the company’s longstanding commitment to transparent disclosure, meaningful investor engagement, and ongoing dialogue with shareholders and analysts.

2026 Extel All-America Executive Team Award Categories and Named Winners:

  • Best CEO:
    Joseph Hogan, President and Chief Executive Officer, ranked #2 in both the Combined, Large-Cap and Buy-side, Large-Cap results in the Health Care Technology & Distribution sector.
  • Best IR Program:
    Align’s Investor Relations Program ranked #2 in the Combined, Large-Cap results and #1 in the Buy-side, Large-Cap results in the Health Care Technology & Distribution sector.
  • Best Investor Day:
    Align’s Investor Day ranked #1 in both the Combined, Large-Cap and Buy-side, Large-Cap results in the Health Care Technology & Distribution sector.

Commenting on Align’s recognition in Extel’s All-America Executive Team rankings, Shirley Stacy, Align Technology vice president, finance, corporate communications and IRO said, “We’re grateful for this recognition from the investment community and proud of the work our teams do every day to provide clear, consistent and meaningful investor communications. That work is truly a team effort, bringing together our communications team and colleagues across legal, finance, clinical, and marketing whose expertise and partnership are essential to our investor relations efforts. Our focus is on helping investors fully understand our strategy, performance, long-term opportunities, and the potential of our business through transparent disclosure, thoughtful engagement, and ongoing dialogue. That commitment is especially important during dynamic and challenging market periods, when clear communication and accessibility matter most. We remain focused on continuing to earn the trust and confidence of our investors.”

In 2025, Align earned the Most Honored Company distinction, with its Board of Directors and Investor Relations Program each ranked first in the Large-Cap category and among the top 10 in the Health Care Technology & Distribution sector. In 2023, Align ranked third for Best IR Team and placed fourth on the Most Honored Company list, with its investor relations program highly rated for credibility, responsiveness, and market knowledge. In 2022, Align’s executive team and IR program received top-tier recognition, including first- and third-place rankings for CEO, CFO, and IR professionals, and second place for the overall IR program. These achievements were especially notable during the pandemic era, underscoring Align’s resilience and dedication to transparent communications.

Survey Methodology:

The All-America Executive Team rankings are based on comprehensive feedback from buy-side analysts, money managers, and sell-side researchers at securities firms and financial institutions, evaluating companies on leadership quality, investor relations programs, and engagement strategies. Extel asks voters to name the best chief executive officers, chief financial officers, and investor relations professionals at the companies in their coverage universes.

For over 50 years, Extel (formerly Institutional Investor Research) has offered highly respected proprietary benchmark research and rankings, providing independent feedback on the sell-side and corporate performance; Extel aims to be the first-choice independent validation source of qualitative market intelligence for all three sides of the investment community and has a global presence spanning Europe, Emerging EMEA, Asia Pacific, North America and Latin America.

Align Technology designs and manufactures the Invisalign® System, the most advanced clear aligner system in the world, iTero™ intraoral scanners and services, and exocad™ CAD/CAM software. CALGARY, Alberta--(BUSINESS WIRE)--CES Energy Solutions Corp. (“CES” or the “Company”) (TSX: CEU) (OTC: CESDF) is pleased to announce that it has successfully entered into an amended and restated credit agreement dated November 6, 2026 (the “Amended and Restated Credit Agreement”), with respect to its syndicated and operating credit facilities (the “Credit Facility”). The syndicate is led by The Bank of Nova Scotia as Agent, Lead Arranger and Joint Bookrunner, together with The Toronto-Dominion Bank, Bank of Montreal, ATB Financial, and National Bank of Canada as Joint Bookrunners, and also includes Wells Fargo Bank, Royal Bank of Canada, and Business Development Bank of Canada. The total size of the Credit Facility has increased to approximately C$750.0 million equivalent. The Credit Facility, which matures on November 6, 2031, is secured by substantially all of the Company’s assets and includes customary terms, conditions and covenants.

“The upsized Credit Facility and improved terms are consistent with the increased size, scale and credit profile of CES, and reflect the strength of our financial attributes and recent rating agency upgrades. The expansion to $750.0 million from $550.0 million provides ample liquidity to support the increased size and scope of our business as we continue to move through our growth inflection phase. The new five-year term locks in current attractive terms and is aligned with our identified business needs, potential expansion opportunities, and return of capital initiatives. We thank the syndicate members for their strong participation in our upsized Credit Facility and for their ongoing partnership,” said Anthony Aulicino, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

Highlights of the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement

  • Total facility size increased by $200.0 million, for an aggregate Credit Facility of approximately C$ equivalent $750.0 million;
  • Single syndicated revolving credit facility of C$ equivalent $702.0 million, with a co-borrower structure allowing for draws in either Canada or the U.S., in either currency;
  • Canadian-based C$20.0 million operating facility and U.S.-based US$20.0 million operating facility;
  • Accordion feature of C$ equivalent $350.0 million; and
  • Removal of the Total Net Debt to EBITDA covenant and improved non-financial covenant baskets, aligned with the higher credit quality and increased size and scope of the Company.

A redacted copy of the Amended and Restated Credit Agreement will be available on CES’ SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca in accordance with National Instrument 51-102 – Continuous Disclosure Obligations, as adopted by the Canadian securities regulatory authorities.

About CES Energy Solutions Corp.
CES Energy Solutions is a leading provider of technically advanced consumable chemical solutions to the energy industry. These products and services are deployed at the drill-bit, at the point of completion and stimulation, at the wellhead and pump-jack to support ongoing production needs, and finally through to the pipeline and midstream market. These chemical solutions are instrumental in allowing the oil and gas industry to maximize returns in an environment of steadily increasing service intensity and advanced technical requirements. CES’ business model is asset light and requires limited re-investment capital to operate and grow. As a result, CES has been able to capitalize on the growing market demand for drilling fluids and production and specialty chemicals in North America while generating strong free cash flow.

Celebrating National STEM Day on Nov. 8 by Helping Students Pursue STEM Careers

OAKLAND, Calif., Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The PG&E Corporation Foundation (PG&E Foundation) awarded $327,500 in scholarships to dozens of students pursuing degrees in science, technology, engineering and math (STEM) at colleges and universities across California and Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs) nationwide.

As communities celebrate National STEM Day on Nov. 8, the PG&E Foundation reaffirms its commitment to building tomorrow's workforce through investments in STEM education and scholarships.

This year, scholarships in the amounts of $2,500, $5,000 and $10,000 are being granted to 57 students from across Pacific Gas and Electric Company's (PG&E) service area through the program.

Since 2012, the Better Together STEM Scholarship Program has awarded nearly $8 million to accomplished students. This contribution is funded by PG&E shareholders and is not recovered through customer rates.

By investing in STEM education, the Foundation helps inspire curiosity, creativity, and innovation while empowering students to develop solutions and technologies that can make a positive impact in their hometown communities and beyond.

Scholarship recipients include Quennel Kempe of Fresno and Caden Kelly of Shingle Springs. Both students attend UC Berkeley. Kempe received a $5,000 scholarship and Kelly received a $2,500 scholarship.

"Receiving the PG&E STEM Scholarship shows me that my community believes in me. The financial assistance and encouragement give me the confidence to achieve my goals and make a greater impact in the future," said Kempe, who is studying computer science. 

"The PG&E STEM Scholarship has given me the freedom to focus fully on my education without the added stress of financial challenges. It also serves as a reminder of the values I want to carry forward, using my education to give back to my community, supporting others and helping make STEM opportunities more accessible for future generations," said Kelly who is studying electrical engineering.

Scholarships are based on academic achievement, demonstrated participation and leadership in school and community activities, and financial need. Recipients may reapply annually for up to five years.

Watch PG&E's video series of past STEM scholar recipients.

"We hope these students discover a path in science, technology, engineering, and math that not only leads to new innovations and breakthroughs but also brings them fulfillment and a sense of purpose. We are proud to support them on their journey as they pursue their higher education goals and dreams," said Carla Peterman, President, PG&E Corporation, and Chair of The PG&E Corporation Foundation Board.

Scholarship recipients must plan to enroll in full-time undergraduate study for the entire 2026-2027 academic year and pursue their first undergraduate degree at an accredited four-year institution in California. HBCU eligibility was recently added after an increasing number of applicants were admitted to historically Black colleges and universities, none of which are in California.

Employees Supporting Local Scholars

In addition to the Better Together STEM Scholarship Program, PG&E's 11 employee resource groups (ERGs) and three engineering networking groups (ENGs) award scholarships to help offset the cost of higher education. The funds are raised entirely from employee contributions through direct donations, fundraising events and the company's employee giving program known as Campaign for the Community. Since 1989, more than $6 million ERG/ENG Scholarships has been raised and awarded to thousands of our hometown students.

About PG&E

Pacific Gas and Electric Company, a subsidiary of PG&E Corporation (NYSE: PCG), is a combined natural gas and electric utility serving more than 16 million people across 70,000 square miles in Northern and Central California. For more information, visit www.pge.com/ and http://www.pge.com/about/newsroom/.

HOMESTEAD, Fla., Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Following the Dodge announcement earlier this week confirming its return to the NASCAR Cup Series in 2027, Kaulig Racing today named AJ Allmendinger and Ty Dillon as the drivers for its flagship Cup initiative. The veteran pairing offers experience behind the wheel as Dodge launches a new chapter in NASCAR while Kaulig Racing embarks on a multiyear building phase as the manufacturer's anchor team.

"We just celebrated the 10th anniversary of Kaulig Racing, and I have never been more confident and excited about our future," said Matt Kaulig, founder and owner of Kaulig Racing. "This is a landmark moment for our organization, our partners and the Dodge brand. From our humble beginnings to being named the anchor team for the fifth largest automaker in the world is an incredible honor and a challenge our team is ready to face."

"Bringing Dodge back to the NASCAR Cup Series is a massive responsibility, and one we don't take lightly," said Kaulig Racing CEO Chris Rice. "We knew we needed to put proven veterans behind the wheel to build this program, and no one knows Kaulig Racing better than AJ and Ty. We are introducing a lot of new parts, pieces and variables into our program, so being able to keep some consistency behind the wheel was important for our inaugural season with Dodge. I look at 2027 like we are pouring the foundation for our future."

Allmendinger, 44, returns to the driver's seat of the No. 16 entry. A veteran across multiple discipline platforms, including victories in IndyCar, IMSA and NASCAR, Allmendinger has served as the cornerstone of Kaulig Racing's Cup and O'Reilly Auto Parts Series programs since joining the team in 2019. Across his Cup Series career, the native of Los Gatos, California, secured multiple victories, highlighted by emotional Cup Series triumphs for Kaulig Racing at the Indianapolis Motor Speedway Road Course in 2021 and the Charlotte Motor Speedway ROVAL in 2023.

"Kaulig Racing has been my home for years, and the belief Matt Kaulig and Chris Rice have placed in me means everything," Allmendinger said. "To be chosen to help bring Dodge back to the NASCAR Cup Series is special for me. I've been fortunate throughout my career to drive a lot of different race cars, but being on the front lines of building a new OEM program with a brand as iconic as Dodge is a unique challenge. We're building something special here, and I can't wait to get to work in 2027."

Dillon, 34, will continue behind the wheel of the No. 10 entry. A native of Lewisville, North Carolina, Dillon brings deep stock car roots and extensive Cup Series experience to the organization. A former champion in the ARCA Menards Series and a multi-time winner in both the NASCAR Craftsman Truck Series and O'Reilly Auto Parts Series, Dillon has established a reputation as a disciplined setup communicator and steady veteran operator across more than 300 career Cup Series starts.

"Opportunities like this don't come around often in a driver's career," Dillon said. "To extend my time with Kaulig Racing and be part of Dodge's return to the Cup Series is a dream scenario. Matt and Chris have built a world-class culture here, and the commitment everyone is putting into this transition is unmatched. Dodge has a rich winning history in stock car racing, and our entire organization is focused on honoring that heritage when we hit the track in 2027."

The addition of Kaulig Racing to the Dodge family restores a storied manufacturer legacy in NASCAR. Dodge first entered NASCAR competition in the early 1950s, earning legendary status throughout the 1960s and 1970s with iconic drivers such as Richard Petty, David Pearson and Bobby Isaac, along with groundbreaking aerodynamic innovations like the Charger Daytona. Multiple Work Programs Underway Across Four 100%-Owned Gold Assets as Company Advances Resource Growth, Mine Optimization, San Francisco Restart and Back Forty Feasibility

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 6, 2026) - Goldgroup Mining Inc. (TSXV: GORO) (NYSE American: GORO) (FSE: 55G) ("Goldgroup" or the "Company") is pleased to provide an update on the various technical studies, exploration programs and drilling activities underway across its four 100%-owned precious-metals assets in Mexico and the United States.

With two producing mines, the formerly producing San Francisco Gold Project and the advanced Back Forty development project, Goldgroup is simultaneously advancing a number of initiatives designed to strengthen its existing operations, expand and replace mineral resources, evaluate a potential restart at San Francisco and advance Back Forty toward a possible development decision.

Javier Reyes, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Goldgroup, commented, "There is a tremendous amount of work underway across Goldgroup with the Company having the advantage of four 100%-owned assets at different stages of the mining cycle, namely, production, development, exploration and discovery."

At San Francisco, we are doing the technical work required to support a potential restart while our 26,000-metre drill program is generating new geological information and testing opportunities for resource growth. At Don David, we are drilling to replace and expand resources around our producing mines while advancing a number of highly prospective regional exploration targets. At Cerro Prieto, we are developing a plan to re-leach the existing leach pads and hopefully extend the asset life. And at Back Forty, our feasibility study is advancing one of the most significant development opportunities in the portfolio.

Importantly, these programs are not isolated initiatives. Together, they are designed to advance additional production opportunities, optimize existing operations, grow our resource base and extend mine lives. We believe this creates a strong foundation for Goldgroup's next phase of growth."

SAN FRANCISCO – DRILLING AND TECHNICAL STUDY SUPPORTING POTENTIAL RESTART

Goldgroup is advancing its 100%-owned San Francisco Gold Project in Sonora through an integrated drilling, technical and mine-planning program designed to evaluate the potential restart and optimization of the formerly producing open-pit operation.

The Company has a 26,000-metre diamond drilling program underway, the first significant new drilling campaign at San Francisco in many years.

The program has three principal objectives:

  • Resource definition and geological confidence – improving the understanding of the geometry, continuity and grade distribution of known mineralization;
  • Resource expansion – testing extensions of known mineralization and additional mineralized structures; and
  • Mine planning and technical studies – generating geological, structural, geotechnical and other information required to evaluate potential restart scenarios.

As disclosed on September 8, 2026, the first results from the program have already demonstrated both higher-grade intervals and broader zones of gold mineralization within areas of known mineralization. Results are being incorporated into the Company's geological and resource models and technical work. Additional results are anticipated soon.

In parallel with drilling, Goldgroup is advancing a complete technical study and mine plan for San Francisco. The work is evaluating the potential restart and optimization of the operation and incorporates updated geological and resource information together with mine planning, geotechnical, metallurgical, processing, infrastructure, capital and operating-cost considerations.

The Company is also refurbishing existing processing infrastructure, including the crushing circuit and ADR plant, in preparation of a potential restart.

The current work is expected to provide an important technical foundation for a development decision regarding the potential restart of San Francisco.

DON DAVID – RESOURCE REPLACEMENT, RESOURCE GROWTH AND REGIONAL EXPLORATION

At the 100%-owned Don David Gold Mine complex in Oaxaca, Goldgroup continues to invest in drilling and exploration around its two producing underground mines, Arista and Alta Gracia.

During the first seven months of 2026, the Company completed approximately 25,726 metres of diamond drilling in 123 holes, including approximately 16,249 metres of infill drilling and 8,794 metres of expansion drilling. More than 97% of the program was directed toward resource definition and expansion.

This work is designed to:

  • replace and expand mineral resources being converted into production;
  • improve geological confidence and mine planning;
  • test extensions of known mineralized structures;
  • identify additional mineralized zones; and
  • support the potential extension of mine lives.

Goldgroup is also advancing exploration across the broader Don David land package, which extends approximately 55 kilometres along the San José structural corridor.

Two of the most important regional exploration opportunities are Margaritas and El Rey.

Margaritas

Margaritas is located northwest of the Arista mine and hosts multiple epithermal gold-silver vein structures. Historical exploration has identified locally high-grade mineralization, and the Company believes the area warrants additional systematic exploration to better understand the scale, continuity and geometry of the mineralized system.

Goldgroup is evaluating the next phase of work at Margaritas, including additional drilling and geological work designed to test the broader exploration opportunity.

El Rey

El Rey is located approximately 44 kilometres northwest of Arista along the San José structural corridor. Historical drilling identified high-grade gold and silver mineralization, providing a geological basis for further exploration.

The Company is working to design an exploration program to test and expand the mineralized system.

Goldgroup believes the combination of near-mine exploration around the producing operations and regional exploration across the broader land package provides multiple opportunities to replace resources consumed through mining while potentially identifying additional sources of future production.

CERRO PRIETO – RESOURCE EXPANSION AND MINE-LIFE OPPORTUNITIES

At the 100%-owned Cerro Prieto heap-leach gold mine in Sonora. Goldgroup continues to operate the mine while advancing technical work on a project to re-leach the existing heaps, in addition to exploration and development drilling designed to expand and improve its understanding of the mineral resource base.

The releaching project considers expanding the heap leach facilities and finer crushing of the existing heaps to recover un-leached gold. This project is supported by a sonic drilling program that is currently underway, which will provide direct samples of contained gold as well as provide material for additional leach testing. The sonic program is made up of 45 drillholes totaling 1,554 meters, of which 26 holes and 1,009 meters have been drilled.

The releaching project could add additional ounces to the end of the mine life of Cerro Prieto while testing additional targets along the trend.

BACK FORTY – FEASIBILITY STUDY UNDERWAY

At the 100%-owned Back Forty Project in Michigan's Upper Peninsula, Goldgroup continues to advance a comprehensive Feasibility Study for the gold-rich volcanogenic massive sulphide ("VMS") project.

The feasibility work is evaluating the technical and economic parameters required to advance Back Forty toward a development decision, building on the project's existing technical work and 2023 Preliminary Economic Assessment.

The study encompasses the key components required for development planning, including mine design and scheduling, processing, infrastructure, metallurgy, environmental considerations, capital and operating costs and other technical and economic parameters.

Back Forty is envisioned as a combined open-pit and underground operation processing a polymetallic VMS deposit, with gold and silver as well as copper and zinc providing exposure to multiple metals.

The project represents an important longer-term development opportunity for Goldgroup and provides the Company with significant North American development optionality.

HRS/BHB-1893 demonstrated meaningful improvements in exercise capacity and patient-reported outcomes, with rapid, deep, and durable left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) gradient reduction at 52 weeks

Data support a highly simplified dosing regimen, with a majority of patients potentially served by the starting dose

HRS/BHB-1893 data across both forms of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and preclinical models suggest potential to address underlying pathophysiology of disease, findings consistent with reverse-remodeling and diastolic benefits

SHANGHAI and SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Hengrui Pharma (SSE: 600276; HKEX: 1276) and Braveheart Bio (NASDAQ: BRVE) today presented data from a 52-week open-label extension (OLE) of the Phase 2 study of the investigational, next-generation cardiac myosin inhibitor HRS/BHB-1893 in patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM). The data were presented at the American Heart Association (AHA) Scientific Sessions 2026.

After the 12-week core period and a washout period, all 42 patients restarted HRS/BHB-1893 for an additional 52 weeks in the OLE. At Week 52, peak oxygen uptake (pVO2) increased by a mean of 2.7 mL/kg/min from OLE baseline; Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Clinical Summary Score (KCCQ-CSS) increased by a mean of 17.3 points over the same period. At Week 52, 79% (33/42) of patients achieved a Valsalva LVOT gradient (LVOT-G) below 30 mmHg, with 90% of patients achieving a Valsalva gradient <30 mmHg at one or more visits during the treatment period. A majority (57%) of patients ended the study on the 40 mg twice-daily (BID) starting dose.

In a separate presentation, Braveheart Bio reported new preclinical mechanistic data and ad hoc analyses of the completed Phase 2 study in non-obstructive HCM (nHCM), suggesting HRS/BHB-1893 improves diastolic function while preserving systolic function.

“These 52-week data suggested the combination of clinical effect, tolerability, and simplicity in dosing of HRS/BHB-1893, which gives us growing confidence to proceed with our clinical development in China,” said Su Zhang, Vice President and Head of Non-Oncology Clinical Development, Hengrui Pharma. “We believe that it indicates HRS/BHB-1893 will be an effective and practical option for HCM patients.”

“These data reinforce the differentiated clinical profile of HRS/BHB-1893, suggesting encouraging efficacy, safety, and ease of use over a longer course of treatment,” said Travis Murdoch, M.D., President and Chief Executive Officer, Braveheart Bio. “The study data also suggest potential reverse-remodeling. Taken together with data presented today on the mechanistic differentiation of HRS/BHB-1893 from preclinical work and the completed nHCM Phase 2 study, we believe that HRS/BHB-1893 could fundamentally address the biology of HCM, including diastolic dysfunction, across both forms of the disease.”

“HCM has long been treated as a disease of obstruction, but the biology is more fundamental, and today's data begin to reflect that reality,” said Theodore Abraham, M.D., Co-director of UCSF HCM Center of Excellence. “These results suggest that it may be possible to engage that biology directly. The evidence of attenuated rebound after 52 weeks points to a treatment that is beginning to modify the structural and biological substrate of the disease. The diastolic findings in non-obstructive patients, consistent across preclinical models and the clinic, show that the same mechanism can improve ventricular relaxation and filling that have historically constrained this class. For patients living with HCM in all its forms, that could represent a meaningfully different kind of progress.”

Long-term efficacy and safety data of HRS/BHB-1893 in patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: results from the 52-week extension period

The Phase 2 study of HRS/BHB-1893 (NCT06516068) enrolled 42 adults with symptomatic oHCM. During the 12-week core period, patients were randomized across three dosing cohorts. Following the core period and a washout phase, all 42 patients entered the OLE. Patients then resumed treatment with HRS/BHB-1893 at a starting dose of 40 mg BID with opportunity for titration to 60 mg or 80 mg BID based on Valsalva LVOT-G and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) criteria.

Exercise capacity and symptoms improved with extended treatment. Peak oxygen uptake (pVO2) increased by a mean of 2.7 mL/kg/min at Week 52 from OLE baseline, with 70% of patients achieving a ≥1.5 mL/kg/min improvement and 50% achieving a ≥3.0 mL/kg/min improvement. KCCQ-CSS increased by a mean of 17.3 points at Week 52 from OLE baseline, with 45% of patients achieving a ≥20-point improvement. 60% of patients achieved New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class I after 52 weeks of treatment.

HRS/BHB-1893-treated patients showed rapid, deep, and durable reductions in LVOT-G. Responders were observed as early as Day 1. By Week 1 (before the first titration), 67% of patients achieved complete LVOT-G response (Valsalva gradient <30 mmHg). At Week 52, 79% of patients (33/42) achieved Valsalva LVOT-G <30 mmHg, and 90% of patients achieved a Valsalva gradient <30 mmHg at one or more visits during the treatment period. 57% of patients (24/42) were maintained on the 40 mg BID starting dose and an additional 19% (8/42) were maintained on 60 mg BID at end of study.

The OLE washout design enabled a post hoc analysis comparison of gradient and biomarker rebound following 12 weeks versus 52 weeks of treatment with matched drug exposure. Following the 12-week core period, LVOT-G and N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP) returned to or went above pre-treatment levels after washout. Following 52 weeks of OLE treatment, signs of reduced disease burden were observed with attenuated return of NT-proBNP and LVOT-G.

HRS/BHB-1893 was generally well tolerated across the 52-week OLE period, with no on-treatment severe or serious adverse events. All on-treatment treatment-emergent adverse events (TEAEs) were mild or moderate in severity and no adverse events led to permanent study drug discontinuation. Two patients had transient reductions in LVEF below 50% (48% and 49% site-measured) and both resumed treatment at a lower dose.

The data were presented in a late-breaking oral presentation, “Long-Term Efficacy and Safety of HRS/BHB-1893 in Patients With Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Results From the 52-Week Extension Period,” by Xueyi Wu, M.D., Fuwai Hospital, Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and Peking Union Medical College, on Friday, November 6, 2026, at 2:15 p.m. CT.

HRS/BHB-1893 improved indices of diastolic function: evidence from in vitro studies and nHCM patients

In a second presentation, Braveheart Bio reported mechanistic and clinical evidence that HRS/BHB-1893 improves indices of diastolic function with minimal effect on systolic performance, suggesting potential to address a therapeutic gap that has limited existing therapies.

The post hoc pooled-dose analysis evaluated effects of HRS/BHB-1893 on cardiac function in HCM engineered heart tissues (EHTs) and echocardiographic parameters for 84 patients with nHCM from the completed, placebo-controlled Phase 2 HRS-1893-202 study (NCT06816251). In preclinical HCM EHTs carrying the R403Q pathogenic myosin mutation, HRS/BHB-1893 was observed to improve relaxation time well below concentrations required to meaningfully reduce systolic force.

In nHCM patients, post hoc pooled-dose analysis showed significant improvements across multiple established indices of diastolic function after 12 weeks of treatment. For septal e', 59% of treated patients exceeded the normal threshold of 7 cm/s, compared to 20% at baseline and 14% in the control group. For lateral e', 57% of treated patients exceeded the 10 cm/s threshold, compared to 21% at baseline and 18% in the control group. E/e' ratio decreased and left ventricular end-diastolic volume increased, which is consistent with a downward shift of the left ventricular pressure-volume relationship and a more compliant, distensible ventricle. Left atrial volume index decreased, reflecting the downstream benefit of improved diastolic filling. Left ventricular global longitudinal strain (LVGLS) was preserved across the treated group, with 39% of HRS/BHB-1893-treated patients versus 15% of placebo patients demonstrating an improvement in LVGLS by ≥10%.

Because patients with nHCM have no obstruction to relieve, these results point to the proposed mechanism of action of HRS/BHB-1893. Across laboratory models and patients, the molecule appears to act on the excess actomyosin cross-bridge activity that drives diastolic dysfunction in HCM, improving ventricular filling while preserving systolic function. Together, the data support the potential of HRS/BHB-1893 as a differentiated, next-generation cardiac myosin inhibitor.

The data were presented in a moderated poster session, “HRS/BHB-1893, a Next-Generation Cardiac Myosin Inhibitor, Improves Indices of Diastolic Function in Non-Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Evidence from In Vitro Studies and Patients,” by Carlos L. del Rio, Ph.D., Senior Vice President, Cardiovascular Research & Translational Science, Braveheart Bio, on Friday, November 6, 2026.

Investor Event and Webcast

Braveheart Bio will host an investor event and webcast today, November 6, 2026, at 3:35 p.m. CT (4:35 p.m. ET) to discuss these data and how they inform future clinical plans, including a planned fixed-dose Phase 2b study in oHCM (TRUEHEART-HCM). A live webcast will be available in the Investors section of the Braveheart Bio website at ir.braveheart.bio, and a replay will be archived following the event.

About Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy

Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a chronic disease estimated to affect more than 700,000 individuals in the United States, and remains an area of significant unmet medical need. HCM can lead to heart failure, stroke or sudden cardiac death, including in young adults and athletes who may often live with the disease undetected.

In HCM, overactive myosin can cause excessive contraction of the heart, resulting in the heart muscle becoming abnormally thick, particularly in the left ventricle, the heart's main pumping chamber. This can lead to symptoms like shortness of breath, chest pain, fatigue and fainting, which typically worsen with physical activity and can significantly limit patients' ability to exercise, work or perform routine tasks.

Approximately two-thirds of patients with HCM have oHCM, where the thickened muscle creates a blockage in the heart's main pumping chamber, making it harder for blood to flow out to the body with each heartbeat. Approximately one-third of patients with HCM have non-obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM), where there is no obstruction, but the muscle is thickened, limiting proper heart function.

About HRS/BHB-1893

HRS/BHB-1893 (designated HRS-1893 by Hengrui and BHB-1893 by Braveheart) is an investigational next-generation oral small-molecule cardiac myosin inhibitor engineered for rapid onset of action, minimal impact on left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) and ease of use. By modulating cardiac contractility, HRS/BHB-1893 aims to address the underlying pathophysiology of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) while maintaining cardiac output.

HRS/BHB-1893 has undergone extensive clinical development, including dose-ranging Phase 2 studies in both symptomatic obstructive HCM (oHCM) and symptomatic non-obstructive HCM (nHCM), multiple clinical pharmacology studies including a bridging study in Australia, and an ongoing Phase 3 study in oHCM in China (NCT07021976). Braveheart Bio entered into an exclusive worldwide license agreement with Hengrui Pharma for the development, manufacture, and commercialization of HRS-1893 outside of Chinese mainland, the Hong Kong SAR, the Macao SAR and Taiwan Region.

About Hengrui Pharma

Hengrui Pharma is an innovation-driven, global pharmaceutical company dedicated to the research, development and commercialization of high-quality medicines to address unmet clinical needs. Its therapeutic areas of focus include oncology, metabolic and cardiovascular diseases, immunological and respiratory diseases, and neuroscience. Driven by a patient-focused philosophy since its founding in 1970, Hengrui Pharma remains committed to advancing human health by striving to conquer diseases, improve health, and extend lives through the power of science and technology.

About Braveheart Bio

Braveheart Bio is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing therapies for patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) and other serious cardiovascular diseases. Its lead product candidate, BHB-1893, is a next-generation oral small-molecule cardiac myosin inhibitor (CMI) being developed for the treatment of obstructive HCM (oHCM) and non-obstructive HCM (nHCM). Braveheart's goal is to improve the treatment options for these patients by enhancing speed of onset, depth of gradient response, systolic safety and reversibility, and by reducing prescribing complexity. For more information, visit www.braveheart.bio.

CHICAGO, Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- IBM (NYSE: IBM), the University of Chicago, the State of Illinois, and Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park (IQMP) today unveiled an IBM Quantum System Two in Chicago, IBM's first quantum computer in Illinois and the company's most advanced system available. Initially located at Hyde Park Labs and hosted by the University of Chicago, the system is fueled by IBM Quantum Nighthawk, the most powerful quantum chip IBM has ever built.

Today, organizations across Illinois are already working with IBM to explore how quantum computing can scale to computationally difficult challenges. The new system aims to catalyze the state's robust ecosystem of scientists, universities, national laboratories, startups, and enterprises, many of whom are collaborating with IBM in Chicago within IQMP's National Quantum Algorithm Center (NQAC) to develop the next generation of algorithms and applications. As the anchor system of NQAC, which was established in 2024 by Illinois Governor JB Pritzker with IBM as a leading member, the new quantum computer will ultimately be moved to IQMP, a first-of-its-kind campus in Chicago currently being built to develop and scale quantum technology and microelectronics innovation.

"IBM is proud to deploy our first quantum computer of IQMP — an IBM Quantum System Two. Today, it can deliver scientifically useful results to organizations across the state of Illinois and beyond," said Arvind Krishna, Chairman and CEO, IBM. "As IBM's first quantum computer in Illinois, the system's deployment marks a milestone for Illinois' quantum community and builds on IBM's partnerships across the state as we expand quantum research across academia and industries."

"I want the next generation of breakthroughs to happen in Illinois and the jobs and opportunity that come with them to benefit the people of Illinois," said Governor JB Pritzker. "With the unveiling of IBM's Quantum System Two in Hyde Park, we are giving researchers and businesses the tool to turn big ideas into real-world solutions. With our growing partnership with IBM, we are building an industry that will give Illinoisans more career opportunities and build a future right here at home."

"The presence of IBM's first quantum computer in Illinois, the company's most advanced system available, is a testament to what's possible when partners across government, industry and academia work together toward a shared vision," said Harley Johnson, CEO of the IQMP. "Today reflects the unique strength of Illinois' quantum ecosystem. We're thrilled to see IBM Quantum System Two at Hyde Park Labs while the Park is under construction, and we're more energized than ever to welcome it to the IQMP, where it will anchor the National Quantum Algorithm Center and further establish Illinois as the global destination for quantum innovation."

"The deployment of IBM's Quantum System Two represents the culmination of a years-long partnership that brought together academia, government, and private industry to usher in a new generation of discovery. I am delighted that this machine is being unveiled here in Hyde Park, where our neighbors and community will have a view into the future," said University of Chicago President Paul Alivisatos.

"IBM Quantum System Two brings another critical capability to Illinois' growing quantum ecosystem and showcases the collaboration that makes our state such a draw," said Illinois Economic Development Corporation President and CEO Christy George. "For companies developing quantum technologies and applications, access to advanced computing systems, leading researchers, and industry partners in one place is a powerful advantage. This investment strengthens Illinois' position as a destination for companies looking to innovate, grow, and help shape the future of quantum computing."

This new IBM Quantum System Two advances IBM's mission to bring useful quantum computing to the world and extends the company's commitment to advancing Illinois as a global epicenter for quantum innovation.

Since NQAC's founding, IBM has helped grow the center into a hub within Chicago where industry leaders work side-by-side with IBM researchers to build quantum applications that can scale alongside technical progress in the field. This includes NQAC Grand Challenge participants Deloitte and AbbVie, who are working with IBM and Northwestern University to build quantum molecular simulation approaches for researchers engaging in drug discovery.

Other Grand Challenges participants working with IBM include EPRI and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (U. of I.) to explore how quantum optimization algorithms could lead to more efficient power grids.

Additionally, research institutions and national labs such as Fermilab are working with IBM in Illinois to accelerate high-energy physics research with quantum and advance technologies for distributed quantum computing. 

IBM is also teaming with leading universities such as the University of Chicago and U. of I. to push technological progress in quantum computing. For example, IBM and the University of Chicago recently demonstrated quantum advantage over leading classical methods using an approach with guaranteed correctness.

Now, IBM's quantum computing technology is being brought physically into Chicago. Through NQAC, the new quantum computer will empower Illinois' quantum community to develop new algorithms and applications that will translate to real-world impact. And it will serve as a catalyst for developing Illinois' current and future quantum workforce. Earlier this year, IBM announced it would establish the FutureNow Chicago center at the IQMP in partnership with City Colleges of Chicago, to bring 750 jobs to the region across AI, cybersecurity, data science, quantum computing and other technologies. 

With the arrival of IBM Quantum System Two, Chicago and the State of Illinois will be cemented as a leading destination for quantum innovation, industrialization, and workforce development.

– PURPOSE 5 Study Findings Highlight the Potential of Long-Acting HIV Prevention Option to Address Persistence Challenges with Up to a Full Year of Protection After Second Dose –

FOSTER CITY, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Gilead Sciences, Inc. (Nasdaq: GILD) today announced results from the PURPOSE 5 trial showing significantly higher persistence—defined as consistent and continuous on-time use—among people starting twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir for HIV prevention as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), compared with those starting daily oral emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (F/TDF). The trial included people in the United Kingdom (UK) and France who would benefit from PrEP. These data will be presented at HIV Glasgow 2026.

Key Highlights:

  • Twice-yearly lenacapavir achieved significantly higher one-year PrEP persistence than daily oral F/TDF, with 85.6% of participants receiving twice-yearly lenacapavir remaining persistent through Week 52 compared with 46.3% for participants taking once-daily F/TDF (p<0.0001).
  • PURPOSE 5 is the first randomized study specifically designed to compare persistence between a long-acting HIV prevention option and daily oral PrEP among individuals not currently taking PrEP.
  • Zero HIV acquisitions occurred among participants receiving twice-yearly lenacapavir during the 52-week study period.
  • Results highlight the potential of twice-yearly lenacapavir to address persistence challenges that can limit the effectiveness of HIV prevention efforts.

Despite substantial progress in HIV prevention, approximately 1.2 million people acquired HIV globally in 2025, according to UNAIDS, underscoring the need for prevention options that better support long-term use and protection. Persistence on PrEP remains one of the most important determinants of real-world prevention effectiveness. Daily oral F/TDF is currently the most commonly used oral PrEP medication globally.

“While starting on PrEP is important, persisting on PrEP is critical to preventing HIV acquisition,” said Professor Chloe Orkin, MBE, Clinical Professor of Infection and Inequities, Queen Mary University of London. “In PURPOSE 5, people in France and the United Kingdom receiving twice-yearly lenacapavir injections were much more likely to keep taking PrEP effectively compared with those receiving daily PrEP tablets. These findings suggest long-acting injections for PrEP may help address a very important barrier to sustained HIV prevention for people who need it. It is notable that the study was able to reach a high proportion of new PrEP users.”

“This study was designed specifically to evaluate one of the most important challenges in HIV prevention today: helping people remain on PrEP for as long as they need protection,” said Jared Baeten, MD, PhD, Senior Vice President, Clinical Development, Virology Therapeutic Area Head, Gilead Sciences. “These results demonstrate that twice-yearly lenacapavir has the potential to help close the gap between starting PrEP and staying on PrEP which can have an important impact on our efforts to end the HIV epidemic in Europe and around the world.”

PURPOSE 5 Results

PURPOSE 5 is an ongoing Phase 2, randomized, open-label study evaluating PrEP persistence among individuals with HIV prevention needs in the United Kingdom and France who were not taking PrEP at the time of enrollment. Participants were randomized 2:1 to receive either twice-yearly lenacapavir or daily oral F/TDF and were followed for 52 weeks.

A total of 267 participants enrolled in the study, including cisgender men (72.3%), cisgender women (7.1%) and gender-diverse individuals (20.6%). 37.8% were PrEP-naïve at baseline.

At Week 52:

  • 85.6% (154/180) of participants receiving twice-yearly lenacapavir remained persistent on PrEP
  • 46.3% (37/80) of participants receiving daily oral F/TDF remained persistent on PrEP
  • The difference of 39.3 (95% CI: 26.66% - 51.41%) was statistically significant (p<0.0001)

Zero HIV acquisitions occurred among participants receiving lenacapavir. One HIV acquisition was reported in the F/TDF group; drug-level analysis at the time of diagnosis was consistent with fewer than two doses of F/TDF per week. Participant retention across both groups remained high throughout the study, with 89.4% of participants in the lenacapavir group and 83.9% of participants in the F/TDF group attending the Week 52 study visit.

For the purpose of this study Gilead used strict protocol definitions of persistence. For lenacapavir persistence was defined as receipt of on-time LEN injection at Day 1/baseline and week 26 (+/- 2 weeks) and on-time follow-up visit at week 52. For F/TDF persistence was defined as dried blood spot (DBS) tenofovir diphosphate (TFV-DP) concentrations consistent with ≥ 4 doses/week (≥ 700 fmol/punch) at Weeks 13, 26, 39, and 52.

Safety

The safety profile observed in PURPOSE 5 was generally consistent with previous studies of lenacapavir for HIV prevention. Serious adverse events were uncommon and occurred in 3.9% of participants receiving lenacapavir and 3.4% of participants receiving F/TDF. Investigators determined that no serious adverse events were related to study treatment. No participants discontinued treatment due to adverse events with lenacapavir. The most common treatment-related events were mild or moderate injection-site reactions (ISRs) associated with subcutaneous lenacapavir administration, and included nodules (67.8%), pain (60.0%), induration (20.6%), and erythema (17.8%).

Addressing a Critical HIV Prevention Challenge

Although awareness and availability of PrEP have increased, persistence remains a challenge across many settings. Daily oral PrEP is highly effective when taken as prescribed, but real-world studies have consistently shown that many individuals discontinue PrEP within the first year of use. By reducing dosing frequency to one dose every six months, twice-yearly lenacapavir has the potential to offer a discreet and convenient HIV prevention option that may better align with the needs and preferences of some individuals more vulnerable to HIV acquisition.

About PURPOSE 5

PURPOSE 5 is the first randomized study designed specifically to compare persistence between a long-acting injectable HIV prevention option and daily oral PrEP among individuals who would benefit from PrEP and were not currently taking oral PrEP. The Phase 2 study conducted in the United Kingdom and France evaluates whether twice-yearly lenacapavir can improve persistence compared with daily oral F/TDF over 52 weeks.

PURPOSE 5 is part of Gilead’s broader PURPOSE clinical development program evaluating lenacapavir across diverse populations and settings with the goal of expanding HIV prevention choice through long-acting prevention options.

About the PURPOSE Program

Gilead’s landmark PURPOSE program is the most comprehensive and diverse HIV prevention trial program ever conducted. The program comprises five HIV prevention trials around the world that are focused on innovation in science, trial design, community engagement, and health equity.

The PURPOSE 1 and PURPOSE 2 trials evaluated the safety and efficacy of twice-yearly injectable lenacapavir to reduce the chance of getting HIV. The ongoing Phase 2 and 3 program, consisting of PURPOSE 1-5 studies, is assessing the potential of lenacapavir to help a diverse range of people around the world who could benefit from PrEP.

More information about the PURPOSE program, including individual trial descriptions, populations and locations, can be found at www.purposestudies.com.

About Lenacapavir

Twice-yearly lenacapavir is approved in multiple countries as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV in adults and adolescents who are at risk of HIV acquisition. Lenacapavir is also approved in multiple countries for the treatment of multi-drug-resistant HIV in adults, in combination with other antiretrovirals.

The multi-stage mechanism of action of lenacapavir is distinguishable from other currently approved classes of antiviral agents. While most antivirals act on just one stage of viral replication, lenacapavir is designed to inhibit HIV at multiple stages of its lifecycle and has no known cross resistance exhibited in vitro to other existing drug classes.

Lenacapavir is being evaluated as a long-acting option in multiple ongoing and planned early and late-stage clinical studies in Gilead’s HIV prevention and treatment research program, including a once-yearly injection for HIV prevention. Lenacapavir is being developed as a foundation for potential future HIV therapies with the goal of offering both long-acting oral and injectable options with several dosing frequencies, in combination or as a mono agent, that help address individual needs and preferences of people and communities affected by HIV. The journal Science named lenacapavir its 2024 “Breakthrough of the Year.”

Indication for Yeytuo® (lenacapavir)

Yeytuo injection is indicated in combination with safer sex practices for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV-1 infection in adults and adolescents with increased HIV-1 acquisition risk weighing at least 35kg.

Indication for Yeztugo® (lenacapavir)

Yeztugo is indicated for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to reduce the risk of sexually acquired HIV-1 in adults and adolescents (≥35kg) who are at risk for HIV-1 acquisition. Individuals must have a negative HIV-1 test prior to initiating Yeztugo.

Important Safety Information for Yeztugo

BOXED WARNING: RISK OF DRUG RESISTANCE WITH USE OF YEZTUGO IN UNDIAGNOSED HIV-1 INFECTION

  • Individuals must be tested for HIV-1 infection prior to initiating Yeztugo, and with each subsequent injection of Yeztugo, using a test approved or cleared by the FDA for the diagnosis of acute or primary HIV-1 infection. Drug-resistant HIV-1 variants have been identified with use of Yeztugo by individuals with undiagnosed HIV-1 infection. Do not initiate Yeztugo unless negative infection status is confirmed. Individuals who acquire HIV-1 while receiving Yeztugo must transition to a complete HIV-1 treatment regimen.

Contraindications

  • Yeztugo is contraindicated in individuals with unknown or positive HIV-1 status.

Warnings and precautions

  • Comprehensive risk management:
    • Use Yeztugo to reduce the risk of HIV-1 acquisition as part of a comprehensive prevention strategy including adherence to the administration schedule and safer sex practices, including condoms, to reduce the risk of sexually transmitted infections (STIs).
    • HIV-1 acquisition risk includes behavioral, biological, or epidemiologic factors including, but not limited to, condomless sex, past or present STIs, self-identified HIV risk, having sexual partners of unknown HIV-1 viremic status, or sexual activity in a high-prevalence area or network. Counsel individuals on the use of other prevention methods to help reduce their risk.
    • Use Yeztugo only in individuals confirmed to be HIV-1 negative. Evaluate for current or recent signs or symptoms consistent with HIV-1 infection. Confirm HIV-1 negative status prior to initiating, prior to each subsequent injection, and as clinically appropriate.
  • Potential risk of resistance:
    • There is a potential risk of developing resistance to Yeztugo if an individual acquires HIV-1 before or when receiving Yeztugo, or following discontinuation. HIV-1 resistance substitutions may emerge in individuals with undiagnosed HIV-1 infection taking only Yeztugo, because Yeztugo alone is not a complete regimen for HIV-1 treatment.
    • To minimize this risk, it is essential to test before each injection and additionally as clinically appropriate. Individuals confirmed to have HIV-1 must immediately begin a complete HIV-1 treatment regimen.
    • Alternative forms of PrEP should be considered after discontinuation of Yeztugo for those who are at continuing risk of HIV-1 acquisition and should be initiated within 28 weeks of the last Yeztugo injection.
  • Long-acting properties and potential associated risks:
    • Residual concentrations of Yeztugo may remain in systemic circulation for up to 12 months or longer after the last injection.
    • Select individuals who agree to the required injection dosing schedule because nonadherence or missed doses could lead to HIV-1 acquisition and development of resistance.
  • Serious injection site reactions: Improper administration (intradermal injection) has been associated with serious injection site reactions, including necrosis and ulcer. Only administer Yeztugo subcutaneously.

Adverse reactions

  • Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) in Yeztugo clinical trials were injection site reactions, headache, and nausea.

Drug interactions

  • Strong or moderate CYP3A inducers may significantly decrease Yeztugo concentrations. Dosage modifications are recommended when initiating these inducers.
  • It is not recommended to use Yeztugo with combined P-gp, UGT1A1, and strong CYP3A inhibitors.
  • Coadministration of Yeztugo with sensitive substrates of CYP3A or P-gp may increase their concentrations and result in the increased risk of their adverse events. Yeztugo may increase the exposure of drugs primarily metabolized by CYP3A initiated within 9 months after the last injection of Yeztugo.

Dosage and administration

  • HIV screening: Test for HIV-1 infection prior to initiating, prior to each subsequent injection, and as clinically appropriate using an approved or cleared test for the diagnosis of acute or primary HIV-1 infection.
  • Dosage: Initiation dosing (injections and tablets) followed by once-every-6-months continuation injection dosing. Tablets may be taken with or without food.
    • Initiation: Day 1: 927 mg by subcutaneous injection (2 x 1.5-mL injections) and 600 mg orally (2 x 300-mg tablets). Day 2: 600 mg orally.
    • Continuation: 927 mg by subcutaneous injection every 6 months (26 weeks) from date of last injection ±2 weeks.
  • Anticipated delayed injections: If scheduled 6-month injection is anticipated to be delayed by more than 2 weeks, Yeztugo tablets may be taken on an interim basis (for up to 6 months) until injections resume. Dosage is 300 mg orally (1 x 300-mg tablet) once every 7 days. Resume continuation injections within 7 days of the last oral dose.
  • Missed injections: If more than 28 weeks have elapsed since the last injection and Yeztugo tablets have not been taken, restart with initiation dosing if clinically appropriate.
  • Dosage modifications of Yeztugo are recommended when initiating with strong or moderate CYP3A inducers. Consult the full Prescribing Information for recommendations.

About Gilead HIV

For more than 35 years, Gilead has been a leading innovator in the field of HIV, driving advances in treatment, prevention and cure research. Gilead researchers have developed 14 HIV medications, including the first single-tablet regimen to treat HIV, the first antiretroviral for pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to help reduce new HIV infections, and the first long-acting injectable HIV treatment medication administered twice-yearly. Our advances in medical research have helped to transform HIV into a treatable, preventable, chronic condition for millions of people.

Gilead is committed to continued scientific innovation to provide solutions for the evolving needs of people affected by HIV around the world. Through partnerships, collaborations and charitable giving, the company also aims to improve education, expand access and address barriers to care, with the goal of ending the HIV epidemic worldwide. Gilead has been repeatedly recognized as one of the top two leading philanthropic funders of HIV-related programs in a report released by Funders Concerned About AIDS.

Discover more about Gilead’s unique collaborations worldwide and the work to help end the HIV epidemic.

About Gilead Sciences

Gilead Sciences, Inc. is a biopharmaceutical company that has pursued and achieved breakthroughs in medicine for more than three decades, with the goal of creating a healthier world for all people. The company is committed to advancing innovative medicines to prevent and treat life-threatening diseases, including HIV, viral hepatitis, COVID-19, cancer and inflammation. In 2025, Gilead announced a $32 billion investment to further strengthen its U.S. footprint to power the next era of discovery, job creation and public health preparedness – while continuing to invest globally to ensure patients everywhere benefit from its scientific innovation. NORTH LIBERTY, Iowa, Nov. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Heartland Express, Inc. (www.heartlandexpress.com) (HTLD) is pleased to announce that Chairman and CEO Michael Gerdin will ring the Closing Bell at the Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square on Tuesday, November 10.

The ceremony will recognize the 40th listing anniversary on the Nasdaq Stock Market and the 48th anniversary as a premier truckload transportation company. Joining Mr. Gerdin on stage will be more than 50 employees including professional truck drivers, founding family members, company leaders, long-term employees, and members of the board of directors.

Mike Gerdin, CEO stated, “It is with great pride that we recognize this honor on behalf of our professional drivers, our supporting employees, and our stockholders for forty-eight years as a company and forty years as a publicly traded company on the Nasdaq Stock Market. Through the years, we have remained committed to and worked hard to deliver ‘Service for Success’ to our customers. That commitment is made possible by our tremendous professional drivers and supporting employees.”

Founded in 1978 by Russell Gerdin and headquartered in North Liberty, Iowa, Heartland Express has built an enduring legacy on a simple foundation: a commitment to safe, reliable service delivered by exceptional professional drivers. For more than four decades, that commitment has made Heartland a trusted partner to retailers, manufacturers, and shippers across the country.

Ceremony and Broadcast Details:

  • Heartland Express Nasdaq Closing Bell Ceremony
  • Tuesday, November 10, 2026 - 3:45 p.m. to 4:00 p.m. ET
  • Nasdaq MarketSite – Times Square, New York City
  • A live webcast of the ceremony will be available at Bell Ringing Ceremony | Nasdaq

Heartland Express is an irregular route truckload carrier based in North Liberty, Iowa serving customers with shipping lanes throughout the United States, Canada, and Mexico. Heartland focuses primarily on regional freight, offering shippers industry leading on-time service so they can achieve their strategic goals for their customers. More information about Heartland Express can be found on the company website at www.heartlandexpress.com.
